passage.title: Sami's Red Kite
paras: It was a windy day in the park. Sami had a new red kite. He ran fast, and the kite went up, up, up into the sky.
Then the wind blew hard. The kite flew into a tall tree. The string was stuck on a high branch. Sami pulled, but the kite did not move. Sami was sad. He sat down under the tree.
Sami’s grandfather saw the kite. He went to his car and came back with a small ladder. He climbed up slowly and pulled the string free. The red kite fell into Sami’s hands.
“Thank you, Grandpa!” Sami said with a big smile. This time, Sami flew his kite far away from the trees.

passage.title: The Ball on the Roof
paras: After school, Hadi and his friend Ziyad played football in the yard. Ziyad kicked the ball very hard. It flew up and landed on the roof of the house.
“Oh no!” said Hadi. “That is my only ball.” The boys looked up. The roof was too high to climb.
Then Hadi had an idea. He turned on the water hose and sprayed water onto the roof. The water pushed the ball, and it rolled down into the yard.
The boys cheered. “You are smart, Hadi!” said Ziyad. Then they played again, but this time they kicked the ball softly.

Why do the boys kick the ball softly at the end?
options: Their teacher told them to kick very softly.

passage.title: Camels in the Desert
paras: **Made for the Desert**
Camels live in hot, dry deserts. Their bodies help them live where there is little food and water.
**The Hump**
A camel’s hump does not hold water. It holds fat. When there is no food, the camel’s body uses the fat. A camel can walk for many days without eating.
**Eyes and Feet**
Camels have long eyelashes. The eyelashes keep sand out of their eyes. Camels also have big, wide feet. Wide feet help them walk on soft sand without sinking.
*Picture caption: A camel’s wide feet help it walk on sand.*

passage.title: Owls at Night
paras: **Night Birds**
Owls are birds that hunt at night. They sleep in the day and wake up when it gets dark.
**Big Eyes**
Owls have very big eyes. Their eyes help them see in the dark.
**Quiet Wings**
An owl’s feathers are soft. Soft feathers make its wings very quiet, so mice do not hear the owl coming.
*Caption: An owl can turn its head far around to look behind it.*

passage.title: Word Clues
paras: A **prefix** comes at the beginning of a word. **un-** means *not*: unhappy = not happy. **re-** means *again*: redo = do again.
A **suffix** comes at the end of a word. **-ful** means *full of*: helpful. **-less** means *without*: careless.
A **compound word** is two small words put together: rain + coat = raincoat.
**Context clues** are words near a new word that help you understand it.

passage.title: The Turtle and the Shade
paras: One hot day, a little turtle found a big rock. The rock made a cool shade, and the turtle rested under it.
A rabbit came by. “Please may I rest in the shade too?” asked the rabbit. The sun was as hot as an oven.
The turtle was proud. “No! This is my shade,” he said. The rabbit hopped away slowly.

Later, the sun moved. The shade moved to the other side of the rock, and the turtle was in the hot sun. He was too slow to move fast. The rabbit came back and pushed a big leaf over him to keep him cool.
“You are kind,” said the turtle. “I am sorry I did not share.” From that day, the turtle always shared his shade.

options: It is good to share with others.

passage.title: The Ant and the Big Rain
paras: All summer, a little ant carried seeds into her home. A grasshopper laughed at her. “Why work so hard? Come and sing with me!”
“The rain will come soon,” said the ant. “I must be ready.” The grasshopper only sang louder.
One day, dark clouds filled the sky, and the big rain came. The fields were as wet as a lake. The grasshopper had no food and no dry place to stay.
The ant opened her door. “Come in,” she said. “Next summer, we will work together.” The grasshopper nodded. He had learned his lesson.

options: Singing is better than working all day.

passage.title: Text 1: Night on the Beach · Text 2: Baby Sea Turtles
paras: **Text 1: Night on the Beach (a story)**

Ali and his father walked on the beach at night. They saw tiny sea turtles crawl out of the sand. “Shh,” said Father. “Let them go to the sea.” Ali watched the babies walk to the waves. He felt happy that they were safe.
**Text 2: Baby Sea Turtles (facts)**

A mother sea turtle digs a nest on the shore and lays her eggs in it. After about two months, the baby turtles hatch. They usually come out at night, when it is cool. The babies crawl to the sea. People can protect them by keeping beaches clean and dark.

options: Both tell how to dig a nest in the sand for eggs.

passage.title: Text 1: Grandpa’s Garden · Text 2: Plants Need Water
paras: **Text 1: Grandpa’s Garden (a story)**

Every evening, Majid helped Grandpa water the tomato plants. One week, Majid forgot. The leaves turned yellow and hung down. Majid felt sorry. He gave the plants water every day after that, and soon they were green again.
**Text 2: Plants Need Water (facts)**

Plants need water to live. Water travels from the roots up to the leaves. When a plant does not get enough water, its leaves can turn yellow and droop. Most garden plants need water every day in hot weather.

passage.title: Brush Your Teeth
paras: **Why Brush?**
Food and sugar stay on your teeth after you eat. If you do not brush, they can make holes in your teeth.
**How to Brush**
Brush two times every day, in the morning and before bed. Brush for two minutes. Brush the front, the back and the top of every tooth.
**See a Dentist**
A dentist is a doctor for teeth. Visit a dentist two times a year.

passage.title: The Best Gift
paras: Fahad wanted to give his mother a gift for Eid. He had only five riyals. “That is not enough for a nice gift,” he thought.

His sister Noura had an idea. “Make something with your hands,” she said. Fahad found colored paper and glue. He worked all afternoon. He made a card with a big yellow sun and wrote, “You light up our home.”

On Eid morning, Fahad gave the card to his mother. Her eyes filled with happy tears. “This is the best gift,” she said, “because you made it with love.” She put the card on the wall where everyone could see it.

passage.title: The Two Goats
paras: Two goats met in the middle of a narrow bridge. Below them was a fast river. “Move back!” said the first goat. “No, YOU move back!” said the second goat.

Then the first goat had a better idea. He lay down flat. The second goat stepped carefully over him. Both goats crossed the bridge safely.

passage.title: Busy Honeybees
paras: **Bees Work Together**
Honeybees live together in a home called a hive. Thousands of bees live in one hive, and every bee has a job.
**Making Honey**
Worker bees fly from flower to flower. They drink a sweet juice called nectar. Back at the hive, the bees turn the nectar into honey. Honey is food for the bees in winter.
**Helping Plants**
When a bee visits a flower, yellow powder called pollen sticks to its body. The bee carries the pollen to the next flower. This helps plants make seeds and fruit.

passage.title: Yusuf’s First Fish

“Fishing teaches patience,” said his uncle. “Wait a little longer.”

passage.title: The Sand Castle
paras: Faris and his little brother built a big sand castle at the beach. It had four towers and a wall made of shells.
Suddenly, a big wave rushed up the sand and washed away one tower. His little brother began to cry. Faris wanted to cry too, but he took a deep breath.
“Let us build it again,” he said, “but farther from the water.” This time, they built the castle near the dry sand. The waves could not reach it, and the castle stood until sunset.

passage.title: Where Does Rain Come From?
paras: The sun heats water in the sea, in lakes and in rivers. The warm water turns into a gas called water vapor and rises into the sky.

When the drops in a cloud join and become heavy, they fall to the ground as rain. Then the water flows back to the sea, and it all happens again. This is called the **water cycle**.
